anchorFacts: The Outfield squeeze for next season. 5 Outfielders for 3 positions.

Danny Horn is your starting CF. A returing MVP and the best player in baseball makes it an easy decision. Darrin Davis figures to be your DH as he remains under contract and showed his numbers did not decline, albiet he was injured. Davis has missed substantial time twice over the past three seasons. Vladimir is entering his peak and put up his best numbers of his career last season. Rates as a clutch perfomer and is essentially who you chose over Peter Busch last offseason.

If those spots are set then you have three players for one left field opening. Desmond Morton is you highest rated prospect with 5 tools and has shown success at the MLB level, Frank Reyna is a power hitter with a mass of potential that also showed success. JR Rosado performed well in his major league experience and had good contact numbers but may trend as a role player in the grand scheme. What is the choice Paulson should make here.

angleRead.name: Tanya Cruz
angleRead.text: I'm standing at the edge of the clubhouse, coffee going cold, watching the outfielders' names get penciled in and erased on the whiteboard. Danny Horn in center is a lock — that's not even a conversation. Darrin Davis at DH makes sense on paper, but the man's missed real time twice in three years, and the numbers staying flat doesn't mean the body holds up. Vladimir's entering his peak, put up career-best numbers, clutch — he's earned his spot. So that leaves three guys for one left field opening, and I keep circling the same question: what does Paulson actually see when he watches them? Desmond Morton's the highest-rated prospect, five tools, already shown he can do it at this level. Frank

plan.focus: The unresolved competition for the final outfield spot and what it signals about the A's direction this off-season.
plan.why: The roster math is clean on paper but the human cost is not — three capable players, one slot, and the clubhouse is holding its breath. That tension is the story.

plan.interpretation: The outfield squeeze is less about talent and more about timing — Davis's health, Vladimir's peak, and three young players all arriving at once. Paulson's choice will signal whether the A's are building for now or for later.
